name: Is It Just Me
tagline: You say what everybody does. Suddenly nobody's the only one.
epigraph: A whiskey with a beer. In 1896, a newspaper thought that was worth a story.
glassware: small stemmed glass (about 90 ml) for the rye, room temperature; tall pilsner glass (about 400 ml), chilled, for the beer
language_row: Wren's Resonance on reading v4: ready. Swap test against the Surrealist (ordinary → strange; here strange → ordinary; no "notice"), the Photographer (no keeping), the Reassurer (no single person, no exit), the Morale Booster (nothing planned) and the Wacky One (nothing invented). 4-grams clean over every pour: "go first", "side by side", "what you don't say", "what you give people", "worth more than", "You make people feel" and "a New York paper" (*The Long Answer*) avoided; the closing line's "tell the joke" chosen over "tell your story" (*Anyway*). One "I", no we/us/our (the lint's v1 "we" error fixed); every "he" is the 1896 man (warnings accepted). No "comedian", no stage, no "queer". History about 45% of yours. ✓
sources: Studio fact card `_studio/fact-cards/boilermaker.md`: *Oxford Companion*, BOILERMAKER pdf 306–307 (the 1896 order and the regulars' consternation, citing the *New York Herald*, 5 April 1896, which could not be found on the page: newspapers.com OCR of that issue read, no matching piece; the Scots and Irish habit; the 1930s name; Billy Rose, 1948; rye and lager on today's menus); HERRENGEDECK pdf 1002 and KOPSTOOT pdf 1143 (dossier only). **Primary:** William A. Spring, "This and That", Yonkers *Herald Statesman*, December 1933, p. 20 ("Dave Ray—Boilermaker and His Helper"), OCR read and saved in `work/jester-regular-guy/`. Drink: *Flavor Matrix* STONE FRUIT pdf 236 (beer as a surprise pairing); *Cocktail Codex* pp. 37, 94–95, 99. Room notes: `work/jester-regular-guy/`.
names_note: **Is It Just Me**, the room's pick (all three): the person's own opener, with the confession inside, answered by the reading's last line. Runner-up **No Joke** (Tomás): Spring's one plain line, but it captions the story more than the person. Also considered: *A Whiskey and a Beer* (would spend the epigraph twice), *Not Only You* (gives away y5), *Strange Drinks* (Wren).
open_items: **Not veto-free: gluten and nuts.** Gluten can't be avoided (the beer is the story). Nuts is Tomás's safe-side call (dried fruit packing; stone fruit and almonds are related, *Codex* p. 37), and the recipe tells the maker to check the pack.
**The 1896 *Herald* article wasn't found on the page.** The story's first beat stands on Oxford pdf 306 alone, in Oxford's words ("consternation", no gloss of the headline "A False Alarm").

**The steep is a craft call:** six to eight hours at room temperature (the *Codex* gives room temperature for infusions of an hour or less, pp. 94–95). The rye must be 45% or stronger (50% preferred); at 40% the pair drops under the highball floor. Rye with apricot is Tomás's pairing; the *Matrix* gives stone fruit with beer.
**No namer for "Boilermaker" is on record** (L2): never "working men named it". The Spring column doesn't coin the name either: "December 1933", never "first".

**Kept out on purpose:** the Kopstoot brim (Wren: a second country's ritual, a drink you perform), the cousins as an argument (two countries, dated later), Prohibition by name, Spring's "queer concoctions", the Irish Car Bomb, and Seinfeld.
